headline: Indian stock markets surge as Sensex jumps over 1,500 points driven by foreign inflows and lower crude oil

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) buying and strong foreign fund inflows supported the market rally.
Lower crude oil prices helped boost overall investor sentiment in Indian equity markets.
Strong buying interest in FMCG and private banking stocks led the benchmark gains.
Recouping of nearly all 2026 market losses occurred following strong November performance.
whatHappening: Sensex surged between 1,450 to over 2,000 points while Nifty reclaimed 25,800 and crossed 25,900 levels.
The Indian Rupee hit a nearly nine-month high of 92.24 per US dollar, bucking the general Asian currency trend.
Bharti Airtel announced an investment of ₹1,200 crore into three data centres in Assam.
Jindal Steel unveiled plans for a ₹15,000 crore investment by 2035 targeting coated steel production.
summary:
Indian share markets experienced a major rally with Sensex surging over 1,500 points and Nifty moving past 25,800 levels.
The market surge was primarily driven by strong foreign fund inflows, lower crude oil prices, and gains in private banking and FMCG sectors.
Additionally, the Rupee strengthened to a nine-month high, while major corporate developments were announced by Bharti Airtel and Jindal Steel.
